PullRequest.Title: ci: pin chat-lib runners to versioned images
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

The chat-lib checks ran on the floating `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest` runner labels. This PR pins them to the image versions those labels resolve to today. When GitHub moves a `-latest` label to a new OS version, the move happens gradually over 1–2 months. During that time the chat-lib checks could switch OS versions between runs.

| Old label | New label |
|---|---|
| `ubuntu-latest` | `ubuntu-24.04` |
| `macos-latest` | `macos-26` (arm64) |
| `windows-latest` | `windows-2025` |

These mappings come from the [GitHub-hosted runners reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners) and the [`actions/runner-images` README](https://github.com/actions/runner-images#available-images). They also match the versions other PR jobs already use, such as `ubuntu-24.04` in `pr.yml` and `macos-26-xlarge` in `pr-darwin-test.yml`.

### Changes
- `.github/workflows/pr.yml`: `chat-lib-linux-tests`, `chat-lib-macos-tests` and `chat-lib-windows-tests` now run on the versioned images. Their job names are fixed, so the check names that branch protection uses don't change.
- `.github/workflows/chat-lib-package.yml`: the manual-run workflow's matrix now uses the same labels, so it keeps running the same checks as the PR jobs. Its job names include `matrix.os`, so they now show the versioned labels.

The other `ubuntu-latest` jobs (Monaco Editor, Telemetry, chat-perf, codeql, sessions-e2e, component-fixtures) are not chat-lib checks and are unchanged.

### Validation
- Parsed both workflow files with `js-yaml` and checked that the three chat-lib jobs and the manual-run matrix resolve to `ubuntu-24.04`, `macos-26` and `windows-2025`: passed.
- Pre-commit hygiene hook: passed.
- The chat-lib checks on this PR will run on the new runners.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull requests whose change detector enables the three chat-lib checks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Linux, macOS, and Windows jobs run independently after `changes`; `pr-gate` waits for all three results, so runner queue/provisioning, checkout, dependency setup, build, and tests are on the required-check critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub-hosted runner scheduling and provisioning for Linux, macOS, and Windows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly three conditional jobs per qualifying PR, up to three concurrently
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three jobs provisioned GitHub-hosted runners through floating `-latest` labels; the diff only selects versioned labels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provisioning and queue time block each job and therefore the required PR gate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repository checkout, Node setup, cache restore, and npm registry access
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One checkout, one Node setup, and one cache lookup per OS job; one unconditional chat-lib npm install per job plus one Copilot npm install only on cache miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical actions and cache/install conditions ran on each of the same three floating-label jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All operations execute serially within each job before build/test completion and are on the PR-gate critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract chat-lib, remove ancestor node_modules, build, and run tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extract, build, and test sequence per OS job
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same composite action executed once on each OS job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These serial commands determine each job's completion time.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A qualifying PR creates exactly three OS jobs, not work proportional to changed files or package count. Each job extracts and tests one chat-lib package.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Up to three OS jobs run in parallel; steps within each job are serial. The diff changes runner labels but neither adds jobs nor raises aggregate concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each job restores one node_modules cache keyed by OS/architecture and lockfile state. On a hit, Copilot dependency installation is skipped; chat-lib still performs one npm install. On a miss, one additional Copilot npm install runs. The macOS cache warmer is explicitly arm64 and the cache key includes `process.arch`; the changed workflow does not alter cache-key logic, and repository evidence does not establish a new miss state from the versioned labels.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that job count, ordering, transitive commands, cache logic, and boundary cardinality are unchanged; low evidence for any performance degradation caused by selecting the stated images.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Versioned images can have different queue or hardware characteristics over time, but the diff and repository provide no concrete evidence of slower capacity, added work, or cache misses; exact hosted-runner timing is external and variable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the runner-label substitutions do not add critical-path work, increase fan-out, defeat a demonstrated cache, or increase concurrency.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: A dispatch starts the three matrix jobs; each job must provision a runner and serially complete checkout, cache/dependency setup, extraction, build, and tests for the workflow to finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GitHub-hosted runner scheduling and provisioning for the three matrix entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly three jobs per dispatch, with same-ref older runs cancelled by the existing concurrency policy
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The matrix already provisioned exactly three hosted runners through floating labels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queue and provisioning time precede every matrix job and affect total workflow completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Checkout, Node setup, cache restore, and npm dependency downloads
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One checkout/setup/cache lookup per matrix job; one chat-lib install per job and one extra Copilot install on a cache miss
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same composite action and boundary calls ran once for each of the same three matrix entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These serial operations must complete before build and tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Package extraction, filesystem cleanup, build, and tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serial sequence per matrix job
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly determines each job's completion latency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fixed matrix has exactly three OS entries and one chat-lib package per entry, unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three matrix jobs may run concurrently; the workflow-level concurrency group cancels an older run for the same ref. The diff does not change matrix size, fail-fast behavior, or cancellation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The same OS/architecture-and-lockfile caches are consulted as in PR checks. Warm hits skip Copilot installation; misses add one Copilot npm install, while chat-lib npm install always runs. No changed cache key or demonstrated negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the matrix cardinality, concurrency controls, boundaries, and commands are unchanged by the label pinning.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hosted image performance and queue depth can vary externally, but no changed code establishes a slower image or greater work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the manual workflow retains the same three-way fan-out and work per job.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all changed files and diff pages for the performance focus. Traced both affected CI workflows through runner provisioning, checkout, cache restore, dependency installation, extraction, build, and test execution. The version pins preserve job count, concurrency, command multiplicity, and cache-key behavior; no high-confidence actionable performance regression or provable shipped-regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
